== Biography ==
=== Tyrone deed: collective Glasgow occupiers, 23 October 2026 ===

The original of Registry of Deeds memorial 71498, volume 101, p.337, deed 18 May 1725, registered 1 June 1741, describes “the Glasgows” collectively as occupiers of an adjoining portion of Cavankilgreen, County Tyrone. No personal forename appears. They are not named as lessees or holders of the seventeen acres granted to John Falls; the stated lives John, James and Mary Falls are his children. The original resolves seventeen against the shorter abstract’s twelve. This is a compatible local family context for [[Glasgow-591|William]] and [[Glasgow-551|John]], not their identification or a parent statement. No parent grade, date, migration or named family member is inferred. Trace the adjoining Glasgow holding through same-place Moore estate/deed succession rather than repeat a search for a missing forename.<ref>Registry of Deeds, memorial 71498, volume 101, p.337; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-KFYZ?cat=185720&i=174&lang=en original register image], DGS 008088382, image 175 (index 174), visually inspected 23 October 2026. [https://irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=71498 Two volunteer abstracts] describe this one memorial and are not independent records.</ref>


'''Earlier Tyrone parentage review, 17 October 2026:''' William Glasgow-591 is assessed as the probable father of John Glasgow-551, and John as the probable father of Hugh Glasgow-548, within the explicit family-history pedigree. These are tradition-based probable roles, not documented identifications of the Scottish candidates, the Leitrim witness or either 1740 Hugh.<ref name="TyronePedigreeReview" />
A [https://www.wikitree.com/photo.php/0/0a/Glasgow-590.pdf History of the Glasgow Family] written by [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-590 William Melanchthon Glasgow] says William was among men from Scotland sent to relieve Protestants during the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Derry Siege of Derry]. After discharge of the troops, William remained in the north of Ireland. Other family subsequently joined him. They were weavers and farmers.

William Glasgow is the earliest ancestor mentioned in  [https://www.wikitree.com/photo.php/0/0a/Glasgow-590.pdf the family history document written by William Melanchthon Glasgow]. The document suggests that William was from the city of Glasgow.
== Research Notes ==
=== Earlier Tyrone father review — 17 October 2026 ===

The family history explicitly calls John a son of William and introduces Hugh, the Tyrone-born weaver, among John’s sons. These are specific parent statements in a continuous pedigree, not parents supplied from a shared surname. The nearer part of that account identifies the Hugh–McCullough family and the younger Hugh’s Pennsylvania household, whose children agree with the independently inspected 1827 will. That household correlation supports the account’s family knowledge without independently proving the two earlier fathers. With the retained generations compatible and no conflicting parent account identified for these traditional roles, William–John and John–Hugh warrant probable local assessments. The preference is for the particular family-history accounts, not an identification with other same-name Scottish or Irish records.

Both earlier father names come from one later family narrative; they are not two independent confirmations. John’s circa-1681 birth is calculated and William’s circa-1655/1656 date is estimated, so neither is corroboration. The 1740 return cannot distinguish the two Hugh householders or name their parents. No contemporary record identifies John-551 or William-591 in these roles. The narrative’s Cameron surname-origin and 1689 military story are unverified and are not used as parentage evidence. William’s selected uncertain Inveresk/Cavers identity and Robert-2462 father hypothesis remain separate. John-3960’s very uncertain placement and the alternative that the two Johns are one person remain unchanged. No mother, wife, new date, migration or exact 1740 identity is inferred.

Two existing unmarked/ungraded father links become probable local assessments. No new attachment, documented/certain upgrade, merge or live WikiTree edit is made. Their child sides contain 47 and 43 pre-1850 profiles respectively; these nested impacts overlap and must not be added. All other parent IDs and grades, including the older Scottish and Leitrim hypotheses, are preserved.

The project-held scan was visually checked; online re-fetch was unavailable.</ref>

=== Earlier maintained research retained ===

The dated assessment below supplies the current probable father grades. Earlier uncertain wording is retained as history; separate identity and maternal limits remain.

<blockquote>
=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-2462]] is the proposed, very uncertain working father of the traditional Ulster ancestor [[Glasgow-591]] and the Cavers Covenanter [[Glasgow-4138]]. This carries the existing possible identity with the Polwarth child [[Glasgow-1605]] into a concrete local family model. The Polwarth index names the child’s father as William Glasgow, and [[Glasgow-2462]] is already attached to that child with uncertainty. The three younger profile accounts are retained as possible stages of one life, not three proved brothers. Neither new father attachment is independent support for the other: both depend on the same child/adult identity and on the unproved identification of the named Polwarth father with the Inveresk man.

The Polwarth child was baptised on 4 April 1658. If baptised near birth, he would have been about 21 at the examination of the Cavers servant in June 1679, 26 at the Ormistoun servant list in 1684 and 31 in 1689. Those are compatible ages for the recorded adult and the later military tradition. The Ulster profile’s circa 1656 birth is explicitly a rough grandson-based estimate, not an age stated by a record; its guessed Glasgow-city origin cannot exclude a Borders childhood. The exact forename and surname, compatible sequence and existing Borders candidate make this a usable provisional life model. Polwarth and Cavers are distinct parishes in different counties, and the chronology supplies compatibility rather than an identifying age match. The Cavers setting is recorded residence/association, not a proved birthplace.

The Cavers man is the leading existing Scottish comparison for [[Glasgow-591]] because the records establish a Covenanter and wreck survivor before the reported 1689 episode, while a probable member of his actual parish survivor group, James Young, appears among survivors said to have reached Ulster. Waddell’s 1886 account says all fifty survivors reached northern Ireland; his revised 1902 account says only some and omits both Glasgows from its named list. The omission does not exclude William, but the revision and late publication weaken the blanket migration claim. The 1684 Ormistoun record also prevents assuming uninterrupted Ulster residence from 1679. The later family history’s 1689 service and settlement remain tradition, not verified military service. No particular crossing, return journey, unit or Irish residence is invented. Its Cameron-to-Glasgow surname-origin story cannot explain a man already called Glasgow in 1679.

The weakest stage is the proposed father’s identity. [[Glasgow-2462]] was born at Inveresk on 20 August 1639 and baptised the next day. He would have been only 18 at the 1658 Polwarth baptism and 16, nearly 17, at the associated Elizabeth baptism in August 1656. Young fatherhood is possible, but there is no marriage, residence or occupation connecting him with the named Polwarth father. An older, otherwise unidentified William is a substantial competing explanation. The named-child clause does not prove [[Glasgow-2462]]’s identity. The regional Polwarth/Gordon household of [[Glasgow-3107]] is a stronger local kinship lead than Inveresk alone, but supplies no father clause for William; no exact brother, uncle or father relationship with James is selected. This inherited father remains a very low-confidence default and would fall away on both new adult accounts if the child/father identification fails. No mother is selected for either adult, and no wife or mother is transferred from the Inveresk ancestry.

The Polwarth child could be a different man from the Cavers Covenanter, and the Covenanter could be different from the late family history’s William. The Hawick father [[Glasgow-2731]] in 1692 and Cavers groom [[Glasgow-3587]] in 1708/09 remain competing later identities for the Covenanter; neither is newly equated with him. The attached [[Glasgow-3370]] entry in 1694 does not independently establish the Polwarth man as her father. If later Scottish records identify the Covenanter continuously there, the family history’s permanent Irish settlement would need reconsideration. Other Scottish William candidates and the possibility that the late ancestor account is mistaken remain open. A missing contemporary Irish bridge is not an exclusion, but the combined identification is especially uncertain. No surname or Y-DNA grouping supplies these missing generations.

Two very uncertain local father hypotheses are selected from existing research; no new original inspection, certain relationship, identity merge or live WikiTree save. Existing child/adult records, vital fields, attached relatives and their grades remain unchanged. Connectivity counts retained profile accounts, including possible duplicates, and describes the selected model rather than a proved pedigree. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#polwarth-cavers-ulster-working-family Full selected model, competing families and source limits]. <ref>Existing reviewed records and public profile citations: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBH-RJS Polwarth William, 4 April 1658, father William: FamilySearch baptism index XTBH-RJS]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYL3-24Q Polwarth Elizabeth, 17 August 1656, father William: FamilySearch index XYL3-24Q]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4437421&tab=this Inveresk William, born 20 August and baptised 21 August 1639, Thomas/Agnes: reviewed Findmypast transcript OPR 689/1]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028558&tab=this Cavers William, examination June 1679, servant at Ormistoun: reviewed Findmypast transcript JC39/22]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028560&tab=this Ormistoun William, October 1684 servant list: reviewed Findmypast transcript PC8/8 and PC12/9A]; [https://archive.org/details/cloudofwitnesses00edin A Cloud of Witnesses, 1714, banished-prisoner list pp.274–276; early derivative source]; [https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590 William Melanchthon Glasgow, History of the Glasgow Family, pp.1–2 and 5; late descendant tradition]; [https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Annals_of_Augusta_County.djvu/21 Waddell, Annals of Augusta County, 1886 p.5 note 1; late blanket Ulster claim]; [https://archive.org/stream/annalsofaugustac00wadd/annalsofaugustac00wadd_djvu.txt Waddell, revised Annals, 1902 p.8; some survivors, neither Glasgow named]; [https://ulster-scots.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/USCN-Covenanters-in-Ulster-Tabloid.pdf Holden and Thompson, The Covenanters in Ulster, pp.6–7; modern secondary associate/route evidence]. These are derivative indexes, reviewed transcripts and later historical accounts; the adult identities remain uncertain.</ref>

In the Scottish Covenanters  Index, a William Glasgow born about 1655 Ormistone, Scotland is mentioned.<ref> William Glasgow born about 1655 in Ormistone, Scotland. Book 23, Volume 9, Pages 473, 483, 673.  Drown, Isabelle McLean, comp.. <i>Scottish Covenanters Index</i> [database on-line]. Provo, UT, USA: Ancestry.com Operations Inc, 2003.</ref>. Covenanters of this period were referred to as [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameronian Cameronians]. Ormiston is about seven miles southeast of Inveresk and Musselburgh, where [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1150 James Glasgow] and [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1148 Alexander Glasgow] lived. This locality comparison is incorrect: the reviewed Ormistoun servant records belong to Cavers, Roxburghshire, rather than East Lothian Ormiston. They provide no seven-mile Inveresk bridge. The circa 1655 age in the derivative index is not an age stated by the underlying record.
</blockquote>


William's estimated birth year of 1656 is very roughly estimated. It is based on the assumption that he was 50 years old when [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-548 his grandson Hugh] was born. Based on his grandson's estimated birth year, William's birth could reasonably been anytime between 1606 and 1670. The document by William Melanchthon Glasgow says William was sent to Ireland as a combatant during the Siege of Derry. Assuming he was between the age of 18 and 45 at that time, his birth would have been between 1644 and 1671.

In the Scottish Covenanters  Index, a William Glasgow born about 1655 Ormistone, Scotland is mentioned.<ref> William Glasgow born about 1655 in Ormistone, Scotland. Book 23, Volume 9, Pages 473, 483, 673.  Drown, Isabelle McLean, comp.. <i>Scottish Covenanters Index</i> [database on-line]. Provo, UT, USA: Ancestry.com Operations Inc, 2003.</ref>. Covenanters of this period were referred to as [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameronian Cameronians]. Ormiston is about seven miles southeast of Inveresk and Musselburgh, where [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1150 James Glasgow] and [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1148 Alexander Glasgow] lived.

Possibly the same [[Glasgow-1605|William  Glasgow (bef.1658-)]] who is born before 4 Apr 1658 in Polwarth, Berwick, Scotland. (16miles)

William may have been a descendant of [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-991 Glasgow-991] and/or [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1095 Glasgow-1095].
